chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Hassan, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Every supplication that does not have praise before it is cut off. Rather, it is the praise, then the glorification. I said, 'I do not know what suffices from the praise and glorification.' He said:

O Allah, You are the First, so there is nothing before You, and You are the Last, so there is nothing after You, and You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing below You, and You are the Mighty, the Wise.
ai.seo_question: What is the required opening praise for a supplication to be accepted?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the structural integrity of du'a by linking it to the recognition of Allah's transcendence through the 'Four Attributes' (al-Sifat al-Arba'). The Imam’s selection of these specific divine names highlights the completeness of worship, ensuring the supplicant acknowledges God's absolute existence across all dimensions of time and space before making requests. This practice reflects the scholarly emphasis on aligning human petitions with divine majesty to ensure acceptance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Hassan, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Every supplication which does not happen to have a Praise before it, so it is cut-off. But rather, it is the Praise, then the Laudation’. I said, ‘What I don’t know is, what would suffice me from the Praise and the Glorification’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘One should be saying,

‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Foremost, so there was nothing before You<sup>azwj</sup>, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Last, so there will be nothing after You<sup>azwj</sup>, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You<sup>azwj</sup>, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Hidden, so there is nothing besides You<sup>azwj</sup>, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Mighty, the Wise’’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Hassan from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Any prayer that does not have thanksgiving before it is incomplete. First it is thanksgiving, then praising.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘I do not know what is enough for thanksgiving?’ The Imam said one should say,

‘O Lord, You are the First, no one was ever before You, You are the Last and there will be no one after You, You are the Dominant and there is no one above You, You are the Inside and there is no one before You and You are the Majestic, the Wise.’”
